_comment: Hand-authored mutation manifest for step 1.5. Each entry is a single local edit to the named seed, true to its TAXONOMY.md bug_type, that changes observable behaviour on at least one input in the seed's 1.4 suite (so the mutant is killed). 'old' occurs exactly once in the seed source; 'new' is the single-edit replacement. Applied one at a time by generate_tasks.py. Genuinely un-injectable (seed, bug_type) pairs are recorded under dropped_pairs with a reason and are not generated.

mutations.note: > becomes >=, so a degenerate single-point range low==high now wrongly raises ValueError.
The low>high validation guard is dropped, so an inverted range no longer raises.
The below-low test is negated, so in-range values are wrongly clamped up to low.
The above-high branch returns low instead of high.
Digits are subtracted instead of added, corrupting the sum.
Accumulator seeded to 1 instead of 0, so every result is one too large (and digit_sum(0) is 1).
< becomes <=, so n==0 wrongly raises instead of returning 0.
The negative-input guard is dropped, so a negative n silently returns 0 instead of raising.
Range upper bound loses +1, so n itself is never counted as a divisor.
The n<1 validation guard is dropped, so zero/negative n return 0 instead of raising.
Counter is decremented instead of incremented, so the divisor count is negated.
== becomes !=, so non-divisors are counted instead of divisors.
a is initialised from b, so the gcd is computed on the wrong pair.
and becomes or, so a single zero argument now wrongly raises instead of returning the other value.
The Euclid step uses // instead of %, so it no longer computes remainders.
Returns b (always 0 once the loop ends) instead of the gcd in a.
Right pointer starts one past the end, causing IndexError on any non-empty string.
!= becomes ==, so mismatches are treated as matches and non-palindromes report True.
The scan guard is negated, so the comparison loop never runs and every string reports True.
The vowel 'u' is left out of the alphabet, so words containing 'u' undercount.
The membership test is negated, so non-vowels are counted instead of vowels.
Appends into words instead of reversed_words, so the result stays empty.
split(" ") no longer collapses whitespace runs, so multi-space input yields empty words.
Loop starts one index too low, dropping the first word of the reversed output.
Returns the original word order instead of the reversed list.
Lowercase letters shift by -k instead of +k.
Modulus is 25 instead of 26, so the lowercase alphabet wraps one position early.
The uppercase branch is dropped, so uppercase letters are left unshifted.
<= becomes <, so 'a' is excluded from the lowercase alphabet and left unshifted.
< becomes <=, so exactly two distinct values wrongly raise instead of returning the smaller.
Guard boundary drops from 2 to 1, so a single distinct value returns None instead of raising.
The 'skip the largest' test is negated, so only the largest is considered and it is returned as the second largest.
The <2-distinct guard is dropped, so a single distinct value returns None instead of raising.
Returns the largest instead of the second largest.
Appends the sub-list itself instead of its element, so no flattening happens.
Returns the original nested list instead of the flattened result.
Slice end loses one, so every chunk is one element short.
The size<1 guard is dropped, so a negative size returns [] instead of raising.
Slice end uses start*size instead of start+size, mis-sizing every chunk.
< becomes <=, so size==1 wrongly raises instead of yielding singleton chunks.
Rotation offset is one too large, shifting the result by an extra position.
shift uses // instead of %, so it is 0 for small k and no rotation occurs.
result aliases seq, so the appends mutate the caller's list (and the return value is wrong too).
The empty-sequence guard is dropped, so k % 0 raises ZeroDivisionError on an empty input.
First occurrence seeds the count at 2 instead of 1, inflating every frequency.
Returns the input word list instead of the frequency dict.
Repeat occurrences decrement instead of increment the count.
The seen-before test is negated, so a first-seen word hits the increment branch and raises KeyError.

mutations.new:
if key in result:
            result[key] = result[key] + b[key]
mutations.note: The else branch is dropped, so keys present only in b are silently omitted.
Shared keys subtract instead of sum.
result aliases a, so the merge writes through into the caller's dict a.
The membership test is negated, swapping the sum/copy branches and raising KeyError on b-only keys.
The added value is drawn from a instead of b.
> becomes >=, so ties overwrite and the latest, not earliest, tied char wins.
The 'beats the best' test is negated, so the running best is never really improved.
The empty-string guard is dropped, so s[0] raises IndexError instead of ValueError.
Returns the count instead of the most common character.
The empty-string guard is dropped, so s[0] raises IndexError instead of returning False.
The first-char underscore test flips == to !=, so a bare '_' is rejected.
The first-char validity guard loses its not, so a leading digit is accepted.
The body scan starts one char too late, so an invalid char at index 1 is not rejected.
or becomes and, so a leading underscore (not alpha) is wrongly rejected.
The divisible-by-400 test is negated, so 2000 is misclassified as non-leap.
% becomes //, so the divisible-by-4 test is wrong for ordinary years.
== becomes !=, so the century rule fires for the wrong years (1900 reports leap).
The century-year rule is dropped, so 1900 wrongly reports as a leap year.
The already-seen test is negated, so the first element triggers an immediate False.
A detected duplicate returns True instead of False.
Iterates the empty seen set instead of items, so duplicates are never detected.
high starts one too low, so the last element is never searched.
<= becomes <, so a one-element search window is skipped and single elements are missed.
Midpoint uses * instead of //, driving mid out of range so the lookup raises IndexError. (A low-high subtraction was rejected: it produces a fixed-point infinite loop rather than a killable mutant.)
The half-selection test is negated, so the search moves the wrong direction and misses targets.
A found target returns -1 (the not-found sentinel) instead of its index.

mutations.old: for j in range(0, n - i - 1):
mutations.new: for j in range(0, n - i - 2):
mutations.note: Inner bound is one too small, so the last adjacent pair is never compared and the list is left unsorted.
The swap assigns each element to itself, so no swapping happens and the list stays unsorted.
result aliases nums, so the in-place swaps mutate the caller's list.
> becomes <, so the list is sorted in descending order.
After a sign, the digit start index is one too high, dropping the first digit (and raising on single-digit signed input).
< becomes <=, so the digit '0' is rejected as invalid.
Digit accumulation subtracts instead of adds, negating the magnitude.
The no-digits-after-sign guard is dropped, so a lone '+'/'-' returns 0 instead of raising.
> becomes >=, so a valid 23:xx time wrongly raises out-of-range.
The range-check guard is dropped, so 24:00 is accepted instead of raising.
Hour bound displaced from 23 to 24, so hour 24 is wrongly accepted.
Minutes are subtracted instead of added to the hour total.
< becomes <=, so equal adjacent symbols are wrongly subtracted (III becomes -1).
The subtract/add decision is negated, flipping every symbol's sign.
The additive branch subtracts, so ordinary additive numerals go negative.
The empty-string guard is dropped, so "" returns 0 instead of raising.
Loop bound is one short, so the final character of the line is dropped.
The doubled-quote escape case is dropped, so "" inside a quoted field is misread as a close+reopen.
The in-quotes mode test is negated, so quote/comma handling is applied in the wrong mode.
< becomes <=, so index reaches len(line) and line[index] raises IndexError.
The non-numeric guard loses its not, so a valid numeric component wrongly raises.
Returns a list instead of a tuple, so the type of the result is wrong.
Parses the whole string s instead of the current component part, raising on any multi-component input.

dropped_pairs.reason: is_palindrome has no special-case guard to omit: empty and single-char inputs are handled implicitly by the two-pointer loop (left<right is simply false), so there is no branch whose removal changes behaviour. Off-by-one/wrong-comparison/inverted-condition cover this seed.

count_vowels contains no relational comparison operator (<,<=,>,>=,==,!=) to swap; its only test is 'ch in vowels' membership, which belongs to inverted-condition (in->not in), not wrong-comparison. No single-edit relational swap exists.

flatten_one_level never copies its input (there is no 'result = list(nested)' to alias), and aliasing 'result = nested' would append into the very list being iterated, raising mid-iteration rather than producing a faithful silent side-effect. No clean single-edit input-mutation is available.
flatten_one_level has no guard/branch/case to omit: empty outer and empty inner lists are handled implicitly by the two for-loops. There is no special-case whose removal a boundary test could catch.

Every validation guard in parse_version is backed by a downstream ValueError: removing the empty-string or empty-component guard still raises via part.isdigit()/int(part), and removing the isdigit guard still raises via int(part). The existing suite only supplies inputs that raise ValueError either way, so no guard removal changes an observable result.
